children: By Elvira Pollina and Amy-Jo Crowley
Infrastructure investors including DWS-backed Mediterra DataCenters, as well as CVC DIF
, are among potential bidders for the data centre business of Italian telecoms and fibre operator Retelit, two sources close to the matter said.

The possible sale comes amid strong investor demand for datacentre assets as companies increasingly require AI computing power and digital infrastructure services - market trends Retelit stands to benefit from five years after it was taken private by Spanish investment firm Asterion.
Germany's DWS, Macquarie and Retelit declined to comment. Asterion, CVC DIF, Mediterra DataCenters were not immediately available for comment.

Nomura, which is advising on the sale, is expected to distribute information memoranda later this month, marking the start of the sale process, the sources said. Nomura was not immediately available to comment.
The business could be valued at €700 million to €800 million euros, the sources said, speaking on condition of anonymity because the matter is private.

Retelit operates 38 data centres across Italy, including in Milan, Rome, Bologna, Turin, Naples and Genoa. It also has edge computing facilities designed to process data closer to where it is generated, according to the company's website.
Retelit's assets are seen as attractive because they are located closer to end users, helping to reduce latency and speed up data processing.
Last year Retelit announced a €350 million plan to expand its datacentre infrastructure, including AI-ready facilities around Italy's financial capital Milan.
